offence_severity: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
number_of_offences: Three offences/counts charged and two were finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the FIR and charge-sheet do not disclose the ingredients to attract the provision of s.420 IPC qua the appellant, as there was no dishonest inducement or fraudulent act by the appellant towards the complainant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses' credibility by examining the FIR and charge-sheet, finding that the allegations against the appellant lacked any element of inducement, fraud, or dishonesty.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 2016; Trial judgment: Not stated; High Court decision: 15.07.2022; Supreme Court decision: 20.03.2024
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: S. Nagamuthu, Sr. Adv., S. Hariharan, S. Sathiaseelan, Amaan Shreyas, Ms. Mannat Tipnis, Anshul Syal, Ms. Bhavana Duhoon; Counsel for the State: V. Krishnamurthy, Sr. A.A.G., D. Kumanan, Sheikh F. Kalia, Mrs. Deepa. S, G. Ananda Selvam, Ms. Lakshmi Ramamurthy
investigation_status: FIR registered on 7th November 2020; charge-sheet filed on 4th January 2023; trial completed: Not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: Not stated; High Court: Order dated 15.07.2022 rejecting petition under Section 482 CrPC; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, order quashed and set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant and other accused persons cheated the complainant by swindling the amounts and that the FIR discloses prima facie commission of a cognizable offence.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the FIR and charge-sheet do not disclose the ingredients of Section 420 of IPC against the appellant, as there is no dishonest inducement or fraud attributed to him, and that the allegations are against accused Nos. 1 and 2.
legal_principle_applied: For attracting the provision of Section 420, IPC, the FIR/complaint must show that the ingredients of Section 415, IPC are made out, including deception, dishonest inducement, and dishonest intention.
precedent_relied_upon: Anand Kumar Mohatta and Another v. State (NCT of Delhi), Department of Home and Another [2018] 13 SCR 1028; G. Sagar Suri and Another v. State of U.P. and Others [2000] 1 SCR 417; Prof. R.K. Vijayasarathy and Another v. Sudha Seetharam and Another [2019] 2 SCR 185; Archana Rana v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another (2021) 3 SCC 751; Deepak Gaba and Others v. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another (2023) 3 SCC 423; Mariam Fasihuddin and Another v. State by Adugodi Police Station and Another [2024] 1 SCR 623
other_sentence_order: Quashing of the FIR and the charge-sheet filed against the appellant.
